episode_title: Episode 44 Hire Smarter: Stuart Kliman & Lieutenant General Todd Leslie Smith All The Difference: Leading Through a Workforce Built on Difference

real_qa.q: What are the four landmines that prevent leaders from achieving target actions according to All the Difference?
real_qa.r: The four landmines are certainty (when a leader is convinced they're right and stops listening), inconsistency (the gap between what a leader says they value and what they actually do, especially under pressure), reactivity (when an emotional trigger pulls someone out of their best sense and they react to stimuli completely differently), and justification (converting a leadership misstep into someone else's fault, which makes the other three invisible and locks leaders into defending choices rather than learning from them). Certainty is identified as the costliest landmine, while justification is described as the most insidious because it is the fuel that powers the other three landmines.
real_qa.requete: All the Difference four landmines leadership

real_qa.q: How does Lieutenant General Todd Leslie Smith define the first target action in All the Difference for leaders managing difference?
real_qa.r: The first target action is knowing yourself, which requires self-awareness as the foundation. Leslie Smith emphasizes that difference doesn't derail teams; unaware leaders do. Leaders must understand their triggers, blind spots, and defaults before they can lead through difference. Knowing who you are empowers other people and allows leaders to set the right conditions by surrounding themselves with people who complement their strengths and weaknesses, such as understanding whether you are a big picture person or detail-oriented.
real_qa.requete: All the Difference know yourself target action

guest.bio_context: Stuart Kliman is a longtime friend and industry peer executive at Building Industry Partners. He collaborated with Lieutenant General Todd Leslie Smith and Susan (third co-author) to write the book All the Difference, which addresses leadership challenges in dynamic markets. The three authors bring complementary perspectives: Kliman's business acumen and industry experience, Leslie Smith's military expertise and landmine metaphor from his role commanding Explosive Ordnance and WMD soldiers across 16 states and 19 installations, and their collective focus on leading through workforce diversity.
